For L_K = mean_k softplus(s_negative_k − s_positive), increasing IID uniform negatives from 1 to 32 leaves the expected gradient unchanged: conditional on a fixed example, parameters and forward-pass randomness, E[g_K] = E[g_1], Cov(g_K) = Cov(g_1)/K. This is a direct Monte Carlo derivation: negative-sampling standard deviation falls √32 ≈ 5.66×, but variability from users, masking and dropout remains. More negatives increase the chance of encountering a hard item without changing its expected weight. Thus, “better discrimination” is a possible optimization benefit, not a stronger population objective or guaranteed HR@10 gain. Candidate scoring/storage grows roughly linearly with K; total runtime grows less when encoder cost dominates. Compare validation quality per GPU-second.

Uncorrected candidate softmax instead minimizes log(1 + Σ_k exp(s_negative_k − s_positive)): at K=1 it equals pairwise softplus; above one, it changes the objective and couples negatives through exponential weighting. Mean pairwise softplus retains a uniform pairwise, AUC-oriented target. [Wu et al.](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) analyze sampled-softmax ranking and hard-negative benefits, but their experiments use collaborative-filtering backbones and differing similarity/sampling choices. Importance-corrected sampled softmax is another distinct formulation; its finite-sample gradient generally remains biased relative to full softmax ([Rawat et al.](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2019/file/e43739bba7cdb577e9e3e4e42447f5a5-Paper.pdf)).

Closest controlled BERT4Rec evidence: [Petrov and Macdonald, §6.2.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.07192) cross negatives {1,4,16,64,256} with BCE, gBCE and uniform sampled softmax on MovieLens-1M. This separates count and loss experimentally, but excludes BPR and an exact 1→32 comparison. No directly matching experiment was located. A useful comparison keeps masked BERT4Rec, scoring, sampling, batches and seeds fixed while crossing mean pairwise softplus versus candidate softmax with K={1,32}; report both fixed-update and equal-GPU-time results.
